title: Conclusions and recommendations

blocks.heading: Conclusions and recommendations
blocks.text: A conclusion answers the question from findings within their limits; a recommendation proposes a feasible response tied to that answer and identifies an implementer. Do not introduce uncollected evidence. For community action distinguish aims, organisation, funding and implementation obstacles: assigning volunteers does not obtain money, and an obstacle needs a matched response and responsible actor.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Conclusion
blocks.text: A conclusion is an evidence-based answer to the research question or judgement about the hypothesis, within the enquiry’s limits. A sample pattern can support a bounded answer, not a claim about all places. Findings are the supporting observations, not interchangeable with the conclusion.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Recommendation
blocks.text: A recommendation is a proposed feasible action linked to the findings and conclusions, identifying who could implement it. Name the practical change, implementer and relevant resource condition. A wish such as “improve development” is too vague to follow.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Worked enquiry connection
blocks.text: Explain which recommendation better fits fictional evidence of repeated water-point breakdowns with a trained maintenance provider available: a provider-led repair schedule or an unrelated poster campaign alone. The repair schedule directly addresses the observed reliability fault and has an implementer. Posters may share information but do not repair equipment; feasibility and continued fault records should be checked.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Organisation, funding and implementation
blocks.text: A fictional storage activity costing N$600 with N$200 available needs N$400 additional resources. Agreeing volunteers and dates organises it; recording contributions funds it. If a required lid is late, the coordinator should arrange a provider-approved suitable alternative or delay use. For a book project costing N$100 with N$40 available, seek N$60 or suitable in-kind materials and use the offered dry room to prevent the stated storage loss. These are project plans, not evidence that either was implemented. A recommendation identifies an implementer and follows findings; a conclusion does not introduce a new result.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect the enquiry to its actual development topic and to Population (7.1) for denominators. Keep an individual record of the real procedure, changes, findings and limits. Fictional models teach the method and must not be presented as the learner’s completed fieldwork.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
